sources.note: 712 BCE: after Sargon II dismembered Melid, Melid city was given to Muttallu of Kummuh; 708 invasion.

notes: Cliopatria has no Kammanu. The page and infobox end in 712 but the list dates Assyrian rule from 708, and the Kummuh page has the city of Melid with Muttallu of Kummuh until Sargon II invades Kummuh in 708, so 712 is the end of the Kammanu line. FIXED (reviewer's finding): the Kammanu page says the land was annexed by Assyria and only the city of Melid went to Mutallu of Kummuh; the first version gave the whole province to Kummuh. The 712 loss is now two events, the province minus the Melid cell to the neo-assyrian-empire and the Melid cell to Kummuh, the dissolve counterpart is the neo-assyrian-empire and both are successors with their lands. The neo-assyrian-empire dossier (me-02) has no Kammanu events (vassalage from 719, annexation 712): route me-02. Both Mutallu entries (Kammanu list 713-708, listed as an Assyrian vassal; Kummuh page Muttallu, king of Kummuh) probably name one man; the pages differ on whose king he was. The Urartian control of the 9th and early 8th centuries and the 12th-century dependence on Carchemish are undated on the pages and not drawn; the Melid page names Tiglath-Pileser I's tribute (reign 1115-1077) without an end and says nothing of Shalmaneser III, so no early Assyrian vassalage is drawn. Sulumal (743-732) is on the page without land. Page budget: two pages, one more (Kummuh) opened for the repair.
